subtitle: How a desert king caught a wandering river and chained it to his city

panels.shot: sweeping high-angle wide over an immense step-sided tank under construction, canal slicing in from a distant river, the king and Od builders tiny yet central
panels.action: Jayasimha Siddharaja stands on a rocky rise overlooking the vast, half-built Sahasralinga Talav at Patan, Od engineers and laborers swarming below among stone ghats, channels and temple platforms under the harsh Gujarat sun.

dialogue.text: In drought-prone Patan, Jayasimha Siddharaja and the Od builders dared a miracle of stone and water — a lake of a thousand lingas to bind the Saraswati to his capital.

i18n.hi: सूखा झेलते पाटण में जयसिंह सिद्धराज और ओड निर्माताओं ने पत्थर और पानी से चमत्कार रचा—सरस्वती को राजधानी से बाँधने वाला सहस्रलिंग सरोवर।

panels.shot: slow push-in from burning sky to parched fields around Patan
panels.action: The landscape around Patan lies dry and cracked; distant farmers lead thin cattle, while the Saraswati River glitters faintly far away, beyond dusty scrub and low ridges.

dialogue.text: Gujarat’s sun was a tyrant. Patan, proud capital of the Solankis, stood between a fickle sky above and the wandering Saraswati far to the north.

i18n.hi: गुजरात का सूरज जल्लाद था। चालुक्य राजधानी पाटण ऊपर बेवफा आसमान और उत्तर में भटकती सरस्वती के बीच जूझती थी।

panels.shot: medium close-up on Jayasimha in court, map spread before him
panels.action: Inside a pillared hall in Patan, Jayasimha Siddharaja leans over a rough ground plan scratched onto a palm-leaf and sand table, courtiers and Brahmin advisers around him, some pointing toward the river’s course.

dialogue.text: Jayasimha, called Siddharaja by the chroniclers, knew that strength needed water more than applause. Temples rose, armies marched, yet the city’s wells sank lower each hot season.

i18n.hi: इतिहासकार जिसे सिद्धराज कहते, उस जयसिंह को पता था, ताकत को तालियों से ज्यादा पानी चाहिए। मंदिर उठे, सेनाएँ चलीं, पर हर गर्मी कुयों की साँस छोटी होती गई।

panels.shot: low-angle medium of Od headman before the throne, tools at his feet
panels.action: An Od master builder, weathered and confident, stands before Jayasimha’s throne with a measuring rope and plumb bob at his belt, while attendants watch the meeting in curious silence.

dialogue.text: So he summoned the Od builders, specialists in earth and stone tanks. In royal grants their names were often silent, but in the soil their work endured.

i18n.hi: तब उसने ओड कारीगरों को बुलाया, जो मिट्टी–पत्थर के तालाबों के उस्ताद थे। फरमानों में उनके नाम गुम रहे, पर ज़मीन में उनका काम अडिग खड़ा रहा।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder from Od builder toward king, intimate court moment
panels.action: The Od builder bows slightly yet holds the king’s gaze, while Jayasimha, in simple regal robes, gestures toward the north, his face intent rather than ceremonial.

dialogue.speaker: jayasimha_siddharaja_and_the_od_builders
dialogue.text: “Bring the Saraswati to Patan. Not by prayer alone, but by channel and craft.”

i18n.hi: "सरस्वती को पाटण लाओ। सिर्फ प्रार्थना से नहीं, नालों और हुनर से।"

panels.shot: wide tracking shot along survey line from riverbank toward Patan
panels.action: Jayasimha rides beside Od surveyors who pace out the land from the Saraswati’s bank, staking a straight alignment, while assistants carry cords and wooden levels across uneven ground.

dialogue.text: They walked the land, not the legends. From the Saraswati’s bend they traced a path of gentle fall, a canal that could run without breaking its own strength.

i18n.hi: उन्होंने भूमि पढ़ी, दंतकथाएँ नहीं। सरस्वती की मोड़ से उन्होंने धीमी ढाल का रास्ता चुना, ऐसा नाला जो खुद की ताकत तोड़े बिना बह सके।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view of canal excavation in progress
panels.action: Hundreds of workers dig a straight, shallow trench through the plain, Od overseers directing teams, while Jayasimha watches from a shaded pavilion set up on a rise.

dialogue.text: The earth opened. Canal banks rose, tamped by bare feet and wooden rammers. Royal will lent coin and guards; Od skill turned it into falling gradients and stable slopes.

i18n.hi: धरती चीरी गई। नाले की मेड़ें उठीं, नंगे पाँव और लकड़ी के मल्लों से कसी गईं। राज–हुक्म ने रुपये और पहरा दिया, ओड कौशल ने इसे ढलानों और मजबूत तटों में ढाल दिया।

panels.shot: medium shot at the canal intake, workers shaping regulating kupa
panels.action: Near the river, Od masons line a circular masonry well-like structure beside the canal’s mouth, with carved stone rings and a narrow control channel leading away.

dialogue.text: At the head they built a kupa, a regulating well. Not all the Saraswati could be seized; the flow had to be tamed, its volume measured, its sudden moods restrained.

i18n.hi: मुहाने पर उन्होंने कुण्ड, कूपा बनाया—नियामक कुआँ। पूरी सरस्वती को कैद नहीं किया जा सकता था; धारा को साधना था, मापना था, उसके अचानक मिज़ाज को लगाम देनी थी।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of Talav site, concentric works emerging
panels.action: A vast square depression grows outside Patan’s walls, terraced with half-finished steps; lines of stone blocks mark future ghats, and raised platforms stand like small islands for temples.

dialogue.text: Where scrub once lay, a geometry of terraces appeared. The Sahasralinga Talav would be no mere pond, but a great square tank, ringed with ghats and scattered with temple platforms.

i18n.hi: जहाँ कभी झाड़–झंखाड़ थे, वहाँ सीढ़ियों की ज्यामिति उभरी। सहस्रलिंग तालाव कोई साधारण पोखर नहीं, विशाल चौकोर टंकी थी, घाटों से घिरी, मंदिर–मंचों से जड़ी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Od mason carving a linga niche in a platform slab
panels.action: An Od mason, seated by a temple platform, chisels a neat circular socket in a stone slab while a small linga lies ready beside him, other workers lifting similar stones into place nearby.

dialogue.text: Later storytellers spoke of a thousand lingas around the lake. The record speaks more softly: platforms and shrines, where ritual and water would meet in ordered stone.

i18n.hi: बाद के किस्सागो भ lake के चारों ओर हज़ार लिंगों की बात करते हैं। शिलालेख हल्की आवाज़ में कहते हैं: वेदियों और मंदिरों की, जहाँ विधि और जल तरतीब से जमे पत्थर में मिलते थे।

panels.shot: intimate mid-shot of women and men laborers at the ghats, city in background
panels.action: Men carry baskets of earth on their heads, women pass stone chips hand to hand; children watch from a distance, as Patan’s walls loom beyond the growing steps of the tank.

dialogue.text: The king’s name would be carved on copper and stone, but the weight of the ghats lay on common shoulders. Men, women, children—each basket carried Patan a little nearer to safety.

i18n.hi: राजा का नाम तांबे और पत्थर पर खुदा, पर घाटों का भार जनता के कंधों पर था। पुरुष, स्त्रियाँ, बच्चे—हर टोकरी से पाटण सुरक्षा के थोड़ा और पास पहुँचा।

panels.shot: close-up on an Od builder’s face as he studies the sky and horizon
panels.action: An Od master builder pauses on the embankment, sweat darkening his turban, eyes narrowed as he gauges cloudless sky and the line of the canal merging with the horizon.

dialogue.speaker: jayasimha_siddharaja_and_the_od_builders
dialogue.text: If the slope lies, the lake will never wake.

i18n.hi: "ढाल झूठ बोले तो ताल कभी न जागे।"

panels.shot: low-angle detail of regulating structures and branching channels near tank edge
panels.action: Near the tank’s upper edge, stone-lined feeder channels split from the main canal, each guarded by small sluice openings leading into different corners of the vast basin.

dialogue.text: They built not one mouth but many. Channels branched to feed the tank’s body evenly, so that the east would not drown while the west stayed dust.

i18n.hi: उन्होंने एक ही मुँह नहीं, कई बनाए। नालियाँ शाखाएँ बनकर फैलीं, ताकि तालाव के तन में पानी बराबर पहुँचे—न पूर्व डूबे, न पश्चिम धूल बना रहे।

panels.shot: dramatic wide shot during first trial flow, canal only partly opened
panels.action: A gathered crowd watches as Od builders, under Jayasimha’s gaze, pull away earthen plugs at the canal; a narrow stream of river water begins to slip through, testing the new channel.

dialogue.text: When the canal first woke, they did not fling it open in triumph. They tested it, a cautious thread of water feeling its way along cut earth and stone.

i18n.hi: जब नाले में पहली साँस आई, उसे जयघोष में पूरी तरह नहीं खोल दिया गया। उन्होंने उसे परखा—सावधान जल–सूत्र, कटी धरती और पत्थर पर रास्ता टटोलता हुआ।

panels.shot: medium of Jayasimha and Od builder side by side watching the flow
panels.action: Standing together on the embankment, Jayasimha and the Od master watch the water curl into the tank’s corner, their faces lit by reflected light from the shallow pool forming below.

dialogue.speaker: jayasimha_siddharaja_and_the_od_builders
dialogue.text: “Not miracle, master. Measure. Let it rise as the stone decrees.”

i18n.hi: "चमत्कार नहीं, महाराज—माप। जितना पत्थर इजाजत दे, उतना ही उठने दो।"

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide showing tank gradually filling over days
panels.action: In a composite scene, different water levels are visible as faint ghosted lines, the tank changing from bare stone to a broad shimmering sheet, ghats now touching the water’s edge, small boats moored.

dialogue.text: The lake did not leap full in a night, despite later tales. Inscriptions speak instead of channels, a kupa, days of watchful flow until Sahasralinga Talav found its level.

i18n.hi: ताल एक रात में भरकर नहीं छलका, चाहे बाद की कथाएँ कुछ भी कहें। शिलालेख नालों, एक कूपा, और कई दिनों की सजग धारा का ज़िक्र करते हैं, जब तक सहस्रलिंग तालाव ने अपना संतुलन न पा लिया।

panels.shot: lively medium shot at ghat: priests, traders, women drawing water
panels.action: At a bustling ghat, Brahmin priests pour libations at a shrine, traders wash their hands, and women fill pots from the clear water, Patan’s skyline mirrored in the calm surface.

dialogue.text: Soon ritual and routine braided together. Lingas bathed at dawn; cattle drank at noon; by evening, the lake’s steps held traders, scribes, soldiers, each bound to this new heart of the city.

i18n.hi: जल–विधि और दिनचर्या साथ–साथ बँध गए। भोर में लिंग स्नान करते, दोपहर में मवेशी पीते, और शाम तक सीढ़ियों पर व्यापारी, लेखक, सैनिक—सब इस नए नगर–हृदय से बँध जाते।

panels.shot: documentary-style medium on an inscription stone near a well in Patan
panels.action: A worn stone slab stands beside an old well in Patan; faint Nagari letters are visible as a scholar traces them reverently with his fingertips in the shade.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, a fragmentary inscription near Patan’s wells still spoke of canals feeding the Talav. Not of sacrifice, not of magic—of engineered water guided into stone.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद भी पाटण के कुओँ के पास मिला टूटा–फूटा शिलालेख तालाव को पोसते नालों की बात करता है। न बलिदान की, न जादू की—पत्थर में बाँधे गए नियोजित जल की।

panels.shot: somber wide of the Talav centuries later, partly silted yet still present
panels.action: A later-age view of the Sahasralinga Talav shows silted steps and ruined small temples, yet a spread of water still gleams in the basin, with villagers using it quietly under a wide sky.

dialogue.text: Floods, neglect, and new rulers weathered its temples and banks, but the basin outlived dynasties. Stone remembered the lattice of channels long after the courtly praise-songs fell silent.

i18n.hi: बाढ़, उपेक्षा और नए शासकों ने मंदिरों और तटों को घिसा, पर घाटी राजवंशों से ज्यादा जियी। दरबार की प्रशंसा–गीत चुप हो गए, पर पत्थर को नालों की जाली याद रही।

panels.shot: reflective low-angle close-up of water ripples mirroring sky and ruins
panels.action: The surface of the Talav ripples gently, reflecting broken shrine outlines and drifting clouds, as a lone Od descendant stands in the distance, silhouette small against the old embankment.

dialogue.text: Jayasimha’s glory faded, the Od names stayed unwritten, yet the lake endures as proof that cities stand first on water, on shared labour, and on the quiet wisdom of measured flow.

i18n.hi: जयसिंह की कीर्ति धुंधलाई, ओडों के नाम लिखे ही न गए, पर सरोवर आज भी गवाही देता है—नगर पहले पानी पर टिकते हैं, साझा मेहनत पर, और नाप–तौल से बहते सधे जल पर।

title_i18n.en: Jayasimha's Lake of a Thousand Lingas
